answers.explanation: Ending abnormally (with an error indication) is part of the service too.
With shared memory the processes access the same bytes directly. With message passing the OS carries the data.
Message passing goes through the OS, which is why it needs system calls like send and receive.
The OS watches for errors in the CPU and memory hardware, in I/O devices, and in user programs.
Batch interfaces run commands from a file with no user at the keyboard.
I/O device errors are one of the three places errors come from.
Scheduling is a resource-allocation job, not file handling.
Both cases count as the communications service.
